utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, if perhaps just before the witness comes in I think we've resolved the questions about the web site and the photo and provided that information this morning to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Is there anything further you want to put on that Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before the witness comes in the Chamber has received the submissions of the Prosecution in response to Mr. Topolski's submission about proofing. Is it convenient at this moment for you to make any brief comments by way of reply, Mr. Topolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: The only comment I would wish to make is we have responded in writing and filed that within the last hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may not surprise you to learn we haven't yet received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm sorry if the Court wasn't anticipating that we would do that, but the response that came from the Prosecution was so interesting we felt we had to respond to it in writing and we did so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that. It means that we will need to await with heightened interest the arrival of the submissions before coming to a decision in the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, if Your Honours would deal with it in that way, we would be very grateful. We have tentatively suggested that there might be thought given to finding some room for oral argument in relation to the matter. An estimate, I think, of some 30 minutes is tentatively suggested. It seems to be a little over necessary for me. I would have thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The idea of oral argument itself seems a little --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: It may well be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- unnecessary to me, given the written submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I would have thought so. What I'm simply doing is alerting you to the fact it is there, but I don't press that. It seems to me the issue is sufficiently joined in the two documents that you will, I hope, shortly have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Topolski. That being so, we should have the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could remind you of the affirmation you took at the commencement of your evidence which still applies. Now Mr. Guy-Smith was asking you questions, and he'll continue now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Guy-Smith: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How are you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. We last were discussing your decision to have a meeting with and an interview with Mr. Lehtinen. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's my understanding that in fact you did meet with Mr. Lehtinen some time in January of 2003. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That meeting was I believe at your home, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was in a hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you met with Mr. Lehtinen, your father met with him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I'm not mistaken, your father met with Mr. Lehtinen for two days, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after his meeting with Mr. Lehtinen the first day, he came home and you discussed with him his feelings about meeting with Mr. Lehtinen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that to be true for the second day also. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you had an opportunity to discuss with your father his meeting with Mr. Lehtinen, you had a meeting with him for two days. True?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That meeting was once again at the hotel. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you had the meeting with Mr. Lehtinen at the hotel, you had no difficulty understanding him, did you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any difficulty with the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so we're sure, for -- I want to take this day by day. The first day the interpreter that you used you were satisfied with in all respects. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't find it necessary to ever correct that interpreter while you were speaking with Mr. Lehtinen about your experiences?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did find it necessary?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those minor words or --

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you sit here today could you tell us, if you remember, any of the areas in which you corrected the interpretation that was occurring the first day that you spoke with Mr. Lehtinen.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second day, once again I take it that particular interview, the one that you had with Mr. Lehtinen, once again that was an interview that occurred through an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The second day I was there on my own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were there on your own the second day, I take it that neither you nor Mr. Lehtinen had any difficulty understanding each other during the interview process.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we go into private session for a moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So with regard to the issue of the subject matters that you discussed with Mr. Lehtinen, for example there was a subject matter concerning you being on the bus before it was stopped. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a subject matter concerning the actual stop of the bus. True?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a subject matter about what occurred after you got off of the bus, while you were waiting. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you discussed as a subject matter the drive to the area that's been called the schoolhouse. True?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened at the schoolhouse would have been another subject matter.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, those are matters -- and I know there are more matters that you discussed with him in terms of subject, but those matters that you discussed with him, those that I just mentioned thus far, those are matters that you discussed with him on both days. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you began to discuss the actual facts as you related them to Mr. Lehtinen, he discussed with you the importance of paying attention to detail, did he not?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you agreed with him that you would supply him with as much detail as you could. True?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He also discussed with you at that time, before you began your actual recounting of the events, how important it was to be accurate. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said that we should be as accurate as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course in terms of being accurate, also that you should be truthful. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And. I know that when you started your testimony here today you took an oath. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time you took the oath you swore to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were speaking with Mr. Lehtinen you had that same idea in mind, didn't you, because of the importance of being accurate, the importance of paying attention to detail? As you were speaking with him you were telling him the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It makes sense to me. Now, Mr. Lehtinen told you of course that in the event that there were any corrections to the statement that you needed to make, that you had an opportunity to do that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, but he may have said that. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. He did indicate to you as you were in the process of this interview and making the statement that you would get an opportunity to review what you'd said to him on January 10th and 11th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware of the fact that when you were making this statement with Mr. Lehtinen that it was going to somehow be memorialised? It was either going to be written down or it was going to come back to you in the form of a printout from a computer?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he impressed upon you the importance of you being able to review the statement and make any corrections. Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember he told you that, in case you reviewed the statement and you needed to make any modifications, that you'd have the opportunity to do that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying this to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember whether or not he indicated to you that after reviewing the statement if you felt there was a need to add anything because you left anything out that you'd get the opportunity to do that? That you would get an opportunity to add something to the statement you gave to him on January 10th and 11th?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last question with regard to his offer to you would be: Do you remember whether he said that in the event there was information that was incorrect in the statement, that perhaps he had misunderstood something you said, that you would have the opportunity to delete, take out of the statement, information that was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. He may have said it, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said, this was some time ago.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your memory concerning those events is not as good as what happened back then. Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "no," I'm referring to the time you were meeting with Mr. Lehtinen and making a statement.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the statement, but I don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember at the conclusion of your interview on the 11th with Mr. Lehtinen that you had an opportunity to review the statement? Do you remember doing that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- for the balance of that year, did you have occasion to get ahold of Mr. Lehtinen to talk to him about your statement?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not in touch with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he leave you a copy of your statement when you two parted company in January of 2003?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he left you in January of 2003 you were fully satisfied, as you indicated by your signature and your attestation, that the information contained in the statement that you made to Mr. Lehtinen was the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the balance of the year 2003, were you still going to kosovo.com, still searching the net with regard to matters that were of interest to you about Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, occasionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "yes, occasionally," was that with the same kind of frequency we discussed before, maybe two or three times a week?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe not that often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once a week? Twice a week? Once or twice a week?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And during that period of time for the balance of 2003, did you come across any information that you found of interest during that time in the way that we discussed last on Friday, information that you would then discuss with some member of your family?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly about torched churches. I talked with my entire family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the year 2003, for the balance of that year, from January to December that would be, did you discuss with your family matters concerning the KLA?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss matters concerning Albanian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once or twice a week, maybe not often as that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from discussing these matters with your family, and by that I mean your brother, your mother, and of course your father, did you have discussions with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We now are in the year 2004. And quickly, for the year 2004 -- quickly, for the year 2004 with regard to your use of the computer, I take it that your answers with regard to the use of the computer would once again be about the same: You were on the computer about once or twice a week. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the Internet. I use my computer every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. My question is with regard to matters concerning Kosovo and your interest in matters concerning Kosovo. You once again were doing the same thing you had been doing before which is something you checked in on because it was something of interest to you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at that time looking at the site that you've mentioned to us before, that's www.kosovo.com?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what other sites were looking at with regard to matters of concern to you as they related to Kosovo during the year 2004?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly Novosti, B92, the TV information from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between January 2004 and June 2004, for that particular six-month period of time, do you recall as you sit here today any information that you found to be noteworthy that you discussed with your father, once again about matters concerning Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the same be true for your mother and for your brother?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And between January 2004 and June 2004, did you have conversations with Mr. Lehtinen concerning your availability for trial?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They talked to my mother afterwards, and it was only then that they called us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say they talked to your mother, I take it what you mean is your mother got a telephone call from somebody at the ICTY and then she called you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, sorry to interrupt. I'm not objecting, but I would like to ask my friend to be careful. The precise matters and logistics of the ways in which various witnesses in all cases come to travel here and come to be here is I think something completely irrelevant and not proper for cross-examination. So the contacts are fine but I don't think we should get into the specifics of how these things are dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To assure the Court and counsel I have absolutely no interest whatsoever in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have my question in mind?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after speaking with your mother, did you have contact with Mr. Lehtinen, you personally have contact with Mr. Lehtinen, over the phone?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not me personally. My father did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all the contacts that occurred with regard to communications between Mr. Lehtinen and your family are conversations that were had between your father or your mother and Mr. Lehtinen or other members of the ICTY to the best of your knowledge. Correct? And by that I'm referring to the time period of January to June of 2004.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before that, from January until June we did not talk to them. Later they talked to my mother in Belgrade. This was sometime in September, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you heard about the possibility or the inevitability of testifying in this matter, I take it your mind went back not only to the events but also to the statement you had made to Mr. Lehtinen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only thought about the event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were comfortable with your statement, were you not, in September of 2004?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand it - and do correct me if I'm wrong - there was some brief contact that you had with Mr. Lehtinen in October. True?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me or my father?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm gathering from your answer it must have been your father and not you.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would happen is your father would have conversation or some kind of conversation with Mr. Lehtinen and then he would tell you what was being said and what was being thought of. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I'm never at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during November, did you have any contact with Mr. Lehtinen or was that once again your father?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not me. The only conversation I had was with the relevant authorities from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I am not interested at all in any information concerning how you were going to get from wherever you were to here. What I am interested in is if during that period of time when you said you had conversation with relevant authorities at the Tribunal you discussed with them any aspects of your testimony, what you were going to say in this room before you arrived.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No such questions were ever asked of us. We were simply told who would be interviewing us and that we should be sincere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were told more than you should be sincere, were you not, sir? You were told, once again, you should be absolutely honest?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That of course caused you no difficulty, because that's a position you've maintained consistently since the very first time you've talked to anybody. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have had before you came to court today at least five separate and distinct proofing sessions with the Prosecution, have you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have I failed in the number? Have there been more?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think there were fewer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In your proofing sessions - and I wish to speak about the very first proofing session that you had - do you remember that, do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day after we arrived here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to give you a date, and that date is Saturday -- that's a day, actually. November -- I believe it's 27th of November. Does that refresh your recollection as to the first proofing session?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in that particular session were you given a copy of your statement to review? That's the statement that you had signed on January 11th.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were given that statement, were you by yourself or were you with your father as you had been in the past?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me, what does "as you had been in the past" mean here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the question might be asked first without that addition, Mr. Guy-Smith. If you want to add it as a separate question, well, you can pursue it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have my question in mind?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first proofing session, were you by yourself?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was that session, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately two to three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your second proofing session, do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the day after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was that session?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in that session -- I'm sorry, in those first two sessions, do you recall when you were talking about the time you were at the hotel with Mr. Lehtinen and your comfort level, that you were comfortable? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first day Mr. Lehtinen was not at the hotel. We met him only here at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were here at the Tribunal, your meeting for your first proofing session, I take it that was a comfortable time? And by that I mean, once again understanding that the subject matter was difficult for you, that you were not under any other stressors, were you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You got to drink some coffee and eat some food and chat with these gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the gentlemen you chatted with are some of the gentlemen who are sitting across from me at the bench of the Prosecution. Correct? And you can look over there and see if you recognise any of them; that's an okay thing to do.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first proofing session that you were involved in, did you correct your statement in any fashion, the statement you made to Mr. Lehtinen?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some minor things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And when you say "some minor things," did that deal with the information that you had given to Mr. Lehtinen about your experiences at the camp?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without telling us for the moment what those minor things were, could you recall for us as you sit here today how many minor corrections you made.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were mostly words such as -- things such as whether somebody wore a beret or not. I may have made a mistake on two or three occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the manner in which you spoke with the gentleman in the first proofing session different from the way you spoke with Mr. Lehtinen when you were discussing subject matters?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they just wanted to know whether they could read my statement or whether there should be any corrections to make in case I had made a mistake before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you had an opportunity to do that once before, had you not, sir? That was on January 11th. Mr. Lehtinen gave you that opportunity to review your statement. Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is something that you did?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we've discussed earlier, we know that you did.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time some -- it would be approximately 11 months ago, you found no need to make any corrections.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not thinking about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Guy-Smith. The 11 months has caught my attention. That seems to be quite wrong, doesn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You know, part of the reason I know I'm a lawyer and not a scientist is often times my additions are incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's nearer two years than one year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think you're absolutely right, Your Honour. My grandfather would be exceedingly disappointed in me, I know that, since he taught me my science. And I thank you for the correction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With that correction in mind, which is in fact important, for some two years your statement had stood as an accurate and viable document concerning your memories of what had occurred in 1998.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that in your first proofing session after you read your statement you made some corrections to some minor details. For example, words such as the word "beret." You gave that as one example. Could you tell us once again how many other and at this point what I'm looking for is the number of minor corrections that you made in that first proofing session.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four times, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your second proofing session -- I'm sorry. I do apologise. After you made these three or four minor corrections in the first proofing session, did you then tell these gentlemen that you were speaking to that apart from these three or four minor details, everything else was correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And certainly, after having now had an opportunity to review your statement on two separate occasions, you clearly were satisfied that it was a complete and accurate recitation of your memory and the events. True?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no need for any further additions.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no need.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the second proofing session that you had, I take it that at that point you were discussing the manner in which you would testify, as opposed to the facts about which you would testify. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time, the second proofing session, did you discuss how the courtroom was set up and what the various functions were of the various individuals in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thereafter you had a number of proofing sessions with Mr. Nicholls, did you not?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just looked over there, and I think you recognise Mr. Nicholls, don't you? And the first time you spoke with Mr. Nicholls was a few days after your second proofing session. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: About an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You met with him the next day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was that session?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: About an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you met with him one more time after that, which was the day after. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That session was how long?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: About an hour, perhaps less than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in each of these sessions with Mr. Nicholls, you at that time discussed with him your testimony, and by that I mean the anticipated testimony you would be giving here at this trial. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You no longer were involved in the generalities of the subject matters then, were you? You were now being asked specific questions.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, concerning my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the specific questions that you were asked you were to give specific answers to. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time when you were involved in this process with Mr. Nicholls where he was posing questions to you for which you were to give him answers, you did not feel the need to correct your statement, did you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think it would be fair to say that from those three proofing sessions that you had with Mr. Nicholls you made no additions to Mr. Nicholls with regard to your statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we did make one or two additions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you sit here today you say you made "one or two additions." And your language is that -- your answer is: "I think we did make one or two additions." What are the one or two additions you worked out in concert with Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were some minor mistakes that I had made when the first statement was given that I did not remember at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were these minor mistakes that are once again different from the mistakes which were minor mistakes that you made which you had corrected but a few days before?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the same kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by that you were referring to words that were contained in the statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't then add other information that you had never discussed before, did you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only regarding the Internet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Which session was that in, the first, the second, or the third proofing session with Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We began during the second session. And then just before I came here we continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was a discussion in process, was it? This was something that was being developed between the second and third proofing sessions?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first -- when you first spoke with Mr. Lehtinen, as we have discussed briefly, you mentioned to him subject matters. And we've discussed a couple of the subject matters that you've mentioned with him. And I would like to expand on that list of subject matters, if I could, and see whether or not you agree that these were further subject matters that you discussed with the investigator Mr. Lehtinen. This is on January 10th and 11th, 2003. Okay?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'd mentioned your travels on the bus, the stop; you getting off the bus, waiting; the drive to the schoolhouse, what happened at the schoolhouse. Thereafter as a subject matter you discussed the drive to the place where you ultimately stayed for some days. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when I say "the place," as a matter of fact you agreed with Mr. Lehtinen to call that place a camp. That was an agreement that you and Mr. Lehtinen had with each other during your interview on the 10th and the 11th of January. Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was a discussion that you had -- a subject-matter discussion that you had with regard to what happened while you were in that place that you agreed to call a camp, and by that I mean where you went when you first got there.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then your experiences in an area that you've called a basement. Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your leaving the basement and going to -- back to I believe it is the house where you stayed for a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your recording of a statement that you made just before you left. Right? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then ultimately your leaving that area, your leaving the place that you called the camp. Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that's a fair list of the areas that you covered in your interview for two days with Mr. Lehtinen?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to want to spend some time with you in those areas. Okay? While you were on the bus travelling, before you were stopped, do you recall whether you saw anybody who you thought might be a KLA soldier on your journey?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many of those people you saw?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "just one," as you sit here right now you're sure about that; right? It was just one and that was the one you testified to I believe it was on Friday, that you just saw one?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have your statement in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to direct your attention to page 3, and I'd like you to take a look at the first, second, the third -- it's the third paragraph. It's the very last section where you say: "After some one hour ... " Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there you indicate you'd seen a number of soldiers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw one. I don't know how many of them the other passengers saw as we passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we're clear and I want to make sure we're on the same page and we're communicating with each other here. You said: "After some one hour of driving with the police officer we could see soldiers in the bushes beside the road." Now, when you say "we could see soldiers," I take it you're referring to yourself and others, correct? That would be the use of the word "we." Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw -- when you were speaking with Investigator Lehtinen, this is a language that you used. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't put this -- these words in your mouth now, did he? When he was typing this up --

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- he didn't try to sneak something by you, did he?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you do remember -- it's fair to say that you were pretty scared during that time?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by that I mean not necessarily the first period of time but certainly by the time the bus is stopped you have a bit of fright about you; I'm sure you do.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that period of time when the bus was stopped, you were so scared about what happened -- I'm sorry, what was happening to you right then that you weren't paying a lot of attention to what was going on now, were you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, that's what you told Mr. Lehtinen, that you were so scared at that point in time that you couldn't give him any details about what had occurred. Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure what time we're going to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was heading for five minutes from now, if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Five minutes from now is as convenient as -- whenever you want me to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after the bus was stopped and you got off the bus and you weren't remembering the details, the last thing that you remember -- I'm sorry, not the last thing, but one of the last things I'm sure you remember, and it must have been a hard thing for you, was that your mother was crying on the bus. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us here that you saw soldiers training a rifle on your mother's back. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did train their rifle -- rifles on her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's something that obviously is a pretty important event in your mind, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that when you spoke to Mr. Lehtinen that you didn't mention this at all?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember whether I did mention that to anyone or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you could, please, if you could take a look at your statement. And I'm referring you to page 4 now. At the top of the page that's U0032179. It's going to be in the first paragraph. You said: "I remember hearing my mother crying in the bus and the soldiers arguing about something with the driver, but then I heard the bus leaving."

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you is: You didn't tell Mr. Lehtinen about this. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it this is also something that you didn't tell Mr. Nicholls about, did you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you recall that you told us that the driver had gotten off the bus. Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm referring Court and counsel to page 72 I believe it is, and this would have been on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you told us that with regard to this whole incident --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Page 72, line 23.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to the following question, "After you were ordered off the bus, the four of you, what happened with the bus?" "A. The driver got off. In fact, he returned to the bus because he had gotten off when we did. And they told him to continue, to go on." That isn't information you told Mr. Lehtinen either, is it?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you saw the driver get off the bus.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he got off the bus together with us, he spoke to them, and then boarded the bus again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand your testimony here right now and I understand your testimony of the other day, but that's not my question. My question to you is: On January 10th and 11th, you didn't tell this to Mr. Lehtinen, did you? You didn't tell him this particular detail of what had occurred.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must have not remembered that. It must have slipped my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you went to the proofing session and you had an opportunity to review your statement and you corrected the minor details as you have told us about, once again you didn't mention that to anybody now, did you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't think it was such an important detail. I wasn't really giving it much thought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, this is a fine time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, we will plan the next break somewhere in the order of 25 past 5.00, if that will help.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Although you may not need all that time, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Hopefully I can put a bit of spring in my step.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Or I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's very dangerous having three of my colleagues sitting behind me at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Don't forget they're friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke with Mr. Lehtinen, do you recall telling him about a conversation that your father had while you were waiting for the Golf car to return?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you recall telling Mr. Lehtinen that that conversation was in one language, not in two? And by that I mean there was -- you discussed with Mr. Lehtinen that your father spoke with somebody in Slovenian, a language that you did not understand.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that your father spoke in two languages, both in Serbian and in Slovenian. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that that once again is those kinds of details that you've told us is not important, and it is for that matter that it was not mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you say "that's possible," once again, you had an opportunity to review the statement that you made to Mr. Lehtinen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I just ask where counsel is referring to when he says --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure. Page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where does it say that he spoke in one language.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you go to the one, two, three, four -- the fourth paragraph it says: "I recall my father talking to the soldier in Slovenian, which I didn't understand."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's all you're referring to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to the questions I asked you previously in terms of correcting your statement, here's an example of where, again, you failed to add information when you were at your proofing sessions with regard to your statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason that you did that, so that we're perfectly clear, is because you made a determination that that was not an important detail. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do you recall in your testimony that you have indicated that you saw Mr. Genov being beaten with automatic rifles, sharp objects, whatever was at hand? Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the school. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once again, that's not information that you gave to Mr. Lehtinen, is it, back in January of 2003? You didn't tell him that.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you have your statement there in front of you, sir.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you would take a look at page 5 in the first paragraph you discussed that -- the beating of Genov.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that paragraph you do not indicate that he was beaten in the manner that you have told us about. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but he was beaten. I didn't indicate with what specifically he was beaten, but the fact is that he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, but my question once again is a little bit different. Now, this is, again, a detail. It's a piece of information that you previously have not discussed with anybody. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that this particular detail, like the other details that we've talked about thus far, once again in your estimation, as you were giving various members of the ICTY information concerning your observations you determined was a minor detail and was not important?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think about that. I didn't realise whether it was important or not. At any rate, I wasn't thinking about that at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you weren't thinking about that at that moment, I take it what you mean is you weren't thinking about how Genov was beaten at the time that you were speaking to Mr. Lehtinen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the vagueness of these questions, which I think mischaracterise the statement. Maybe my friend could read the first sentence of the second paragraph, which describes the beating of Genov.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You may read the entirety -- excuse me, Your Honour. My point is a simple point, which is the precise manner in which this occurred according to this witness during this trial is totally absent from this statement, and it is that which I am driving at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that point has been very well-made.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then I am moving on to another point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh, good.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no desire to continue on this point anymore. The point has been made and I move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall in your meeting with Mr. Lehtinen that you were shown a series of photographs?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were shown photographs of people who you believe that you were with while in the basement area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of those individuals, you told us here, was an individual who had been shot in the leg. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't tell that to Mr. Lehtinen, did you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You figured that was another minor detail. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with regard to your identification of individuals who you saw at the camp, you indicated that you were a hundred per cent sure with regard to a number of the people that you saw. Right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say that you were a hundred per cent sure, you don't entertain the possibility of any doubt. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sure only about one person, that is that only one person was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, as a matter of fact, when you spoke to Mr. Lehtinen you told us -- I'm sorry, you told him with regard to the pictures that you were shown that you were a hundred per cent sure that a man by the name of Genov was there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me about the prisoners, yes, I'm a hundred per cent sure that they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what I'm saying is with regard to each and every one of the identifications you made, you have no doubts in your mind about those identifications. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I can identify them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The information that you've given us here in this Tribunal concerning those individuals, which you have not told anybody about before, is information that you decided to edit out of your previous interviews. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm -- I don't want to object, but I think this line of cross is just getting a little bit absurd. We've got before today 120 pages of transcript about this witness's testimony here in court, about half of that probably him speaking. The statement is I think 11 pages of text. So I think it's a bit pointless to continue to claim that every little detail in -- over two days of testimony or about two days is not present in this 11-page statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. It's a very fine point to make in closing address. We're not at the moment limiting Mr. Guy-Smith, but I think he will have got the point of what you've put.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke to Mr. Lehtinen, you told Mr. Lehtinen that you couldn't remember many details about the time in the basement, did you not?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you could remember was that you were scared and that the place was horrible?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us here that you played chess with Shala.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent an hour at a minimum playing chess with Shala.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he was the only individual out of the 50 or 60 soldiers that you saw at the camp whose nickname you ever heard?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remembered him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard the nickname Murrizi?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the individual who you claim was with Shala when he came to the basement door to feed you, can you describe that individual in any fashion other than young?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's all I can remember at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the basement and were in the room playing chess with Shala, this was an important point in your life. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean an important point in my life?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you left the basement you initially thought that you were going to be killed?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you found yourself eating, drinking, playing chess.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly memorable events because they were an indication to you then that you were not going to be killed?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Important details?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't tell Mr. Lehtinen about playing chess with Shala, did you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I did. If this is what is stated in the statement, then that is correct. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've said two things and I want to make sure that we're accurate here. You said you didn't think that you did. I suggest you take a look at the eighth page of your statement, and it would be -- it's kind of the middle of the third paragraph that says: "Then during one day ... " Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have it on -- I'm not sure what version you're looking at at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He's looking at the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that version on page 7 then, "then during one day" is where it starts. There is no mention of this chess game, is there?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no mention of spending an hour with Shala face to face, is there?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact what you say occurred in your statement - once again, if you would take a look at it - is markedly different from what you told us happened here in court, and by that I mean that when you were taken out of the basement you asked if your father could come with you and you said yes.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't ask me right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were reading your statement and you had the opportunity to correct your statement either with Mr. Lehtinen or with Mr. Nicholls, you chose not to correct your statement with regard to this important detail, did you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall telling us about spending some time after you had been released from the basement with an Albanian who discussed with you that he was hiding because the Serbs had killed his lambs?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any discussion with them. It was just later that they told us why he had been in hiding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a minor detail. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why you didn't tell anybody about it before coming to court. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke to Mr. Lehtinen you gave Mr. Lehtinen a description of this man named Shala. True?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you testified in court, you gave a relatively similar description but you left out one part, which is you told Mr. Lehtinen that Shala was "strongly built."

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was on the stocky side. I don't understand quite what you mean when you say "he was strongly built." He was stronger than me, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you don't understand what I said when I said "strongly built." Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I do understand what you say, but I don't know what the difference is between what I stated in my statement and what I indicated in my testimony on Friday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In your testimony on Friday, take it from me, you never mentioned that he was strongly built.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement that you made to Mr. Lehtinen, the individual you describe as Shala was somebody you said was strongly built.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Strongly built is somebody who, as you've just put it, is stocky. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This man Shala who you had all these experiences with, he was a strong man, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A healthy man?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you came to court today -- or actually, before you came to court to testify, you were told that the people who the Prosecution believe are responsible would be in court, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were shown pictures by Mr. Lehtinen, pictures in which you were asked to identify people other than those you've called prisoners, Mr. Lehtinen asked you whether or not you recognised any of the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't just show you a series of pictures and say, Can you pick anybody out who you might be familiar with, did he?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He said -- he asked if I recognised anyone on those pictures. There were eight pictures in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my question is more specific, which is the language that he used with you at the time he asked you to make these identifications was whether you recognised any perpetrators. He focused you in identifying someone who he believed was responsible, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If he knows he can answer it, Your Honour. If he doesn't, he can reject it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I can tell you right now and nobody knows what's in Mr. Lehtinen's mind or what Mr. Lehtinen believed. He's answered the question. The question was put to him: "You were asked to identify people other than those you've called prisoners. Mr. Lehtinen asked you whether or not you recognised any of the perpetrators. "A. Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The tail-end of your question is the one that was the problem. You can proceed from where you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not asking if he's a psychologist, but if he has an opinion with regard to the issue -- and I'm happy to proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Move along, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were shown those pictures of individuals who Mr. Lehtinen said were any of the perpetrators in this case, do you recall how you were showed those pictures? And by that I mean, was each sheet handed to you individually?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were eight pictures on a single page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you handed each page individually?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked at the page, at any one of the pages, what you did was you compared all of the photographs on the page initially, before you chose or didn't chose any of the individuals on the line-up. Correct?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I made it -- immediately pointed my finger at the person I recognised. I didn't think about it much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look at any of the other pictures then?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I pointed my finger at the person I knew, I had a look at the other pictures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So before you took your finger and you pointed at that one picture, you looked at the other pictures, too, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm obliged. Cross-examined by Mr. Mansfield:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I want to ask you some questions about the photograph that you identified from a web site. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that you first saw that photograph on a web site in 1999?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The same column of soldiers was shown every day on the news after our release.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So can we take it slowly. After your release in 1998, you saw the -- that photograph on television before you left Kosovo. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as soon as we were released, the very same day we left Kosovo. But two or three days later there was picture broadcast on the news of their troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Was the picture received by you in the place where you were then living?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was on the news, on TV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw that picture, I think you have said, every day on the news in 1998 and into 1999. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for a month after our release. I saw it again later on the Internet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you saw it every day for a month in 1998 shortly after your release and then you see it again on the Internet.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask -- I understand, you say yes to that. Now, dealing with this as stage one, did you mention anything to your father about the photograph you'd seen on the news?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were together when it was on the news.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do appreciate your father has already given evidence, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know this has been brought up before, but I strongly object to witnesses' evidence being put to other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I would like and appreciate if Mr. Nicholls would be patient, because I wasn't going to put anything at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's fine. We have been going down this line in the past and I put Counsel on notice that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Not with me you haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Please carry on, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are aware that your father has already given evidence, is that right, to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to you, your father saw this picture on television. And what was your father's reaction to the picture on television when you saw it together?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me if I was able to recognise that person, if I remembered that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you say?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course you remember. What did he say?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing of importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he recognise the picture on television?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He did. So he would have been in a position when seen by investigators to say that he had seen this man before on television, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he had in fact said that or not because I was not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask that. He would have been in a position, according to you, to identify to investigators the man he'd seen on television, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stage two. The same photograph, you say, then appears on a web site in 1999. Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it in 1999. I don't know how long it had been posted on the Internet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it you remember seeing it in 1999? Or was it 2000, or was it 2001? How do you remember it was 1999 that you saw it on the Internet?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that is when I bought a computer for my school, and that's I got hooked on the Internet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to summarise the position, if you wouldn't mind listening, of your evidence so far, that between the autumn of 1999 when you obtained a computer and January 2003 when you were first seen by investigators in this case, you accessed this web site approximately twice a week. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will appreciate, therefore, that that adds up to well over 300 occasions that you accessed this web site. Do you appreciate that? A minimum.

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the -- those occasions that you accessed, you would have seen this photograph on many occasions on the web site. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mention that to your father, that you'd seen it, the same photograph from television, appearing on the web site?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to come therefore to stage three, January 2003, when you saw the investigator. You have already said this afternoon that the investigator wanted as much detail as you could give and as accurately as you could give it. That's the position, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked for the details that I was able to remember and also to be as accurate as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you gave at that stage a description of the man who you described as the commander, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: (REDACTED) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
